q: Does a kWh indicator on an induction furnace actually save power?
title: kWh integrator on an induction furnace
short: Only if operators use it. BEE's Punjab foundry report expects 20 kWh less per tonne, 580 down to 560, by setting a kWh target for each melt and tapping on time: 7,200 kWh a year on 360 t, about 4.9 t CO2. It costs about Rs 38,000 and paid back in 1.05 years (2011).
audience: Foundry owners in Batala, Jalandhar, Ludhiana and similar clusters melting cast iron in medium frequency induction furnaces

p: An integrator reads the inverter's output power and adds it up through the melt. You set the kWh a melt should take, based on your best past melts, and it shows how many units are left. The operator taps when the metal is ready, instead of holding it while moulds or samples catch up.

ul: Power was changed often because of empty crucible space, excess charge and waiting for sample analysis.
For 35 to 40% of the heat time the furnace ran at 70 to 80% of rated power.
Charges were made up by experience rather than weighed to a recipe.
Units per tonne varied by 50 to 80 from melt to melt.

sections.h: A number in the report to question
p: The report says the lowest consumption achieved was 650 units per tonne, yet it sets the baseline at 580 and the target at 560. Both cannot describe the same furnace. Use your own meter: take the lowest kWh per tonne of your last 30 melts as the target, not the report's figure.

ul: Write each melt's kWh and tapped weight in a log; the integrator's reading alone is lost at the next melt.
Plan moulding so metal is not held in the furnace waiting for boxes.
Review the month's kWh per tonne with the melting supervisor.

example.title: 360 t a year, before and after
lines: Before: 580 kWh x 360 t = 208,800 kWh x 0.675 = 140.9 t CO2
Saved: 7,200 kWh, about 4.9 t CO2; 13.5 kg CO2 on every tonne
Money at the report's Rs 5 per kWh: Rs 36,000 a year against Rs 37,752 spent
example.note: Grid factor 0.675 kg CO2 per kWh (CEA, FY 2025-26), an estimate. The report's 5.83 t used an older factor.

senseible: Senseible reads your power bills into monthly kWh and CO2. Divide by tonnes tapped and you can see whether the integrator target is holding month to month. The calculators turn your own kWh per tonne into CO2 per tonne.
